title: Stiff-Leg Dumbbell Deadlift
summary: A dumbbell hinge with straighter legs, for the hamstrings.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for hamstrings (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly hamstrings total.
Library rating 0.6 for glutes (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.6 for lower back (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly lower back total.
Library rating 0.3 for forearms (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly forearms total.
Library rating 0.3 for adductors (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly adductors total.

setup.text: Hold the dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Keep your legs nearly straight and push your hips back.
Lower the weights along your legs until your hamstrings are stretched.
Squeeze your glutes and stand up.

form_cues.cue: Keep the dumbbells close to your legs
Return by driving the hips forward
Keep your back flat. Only go as low as your hamstrings allow.

mistakes.text: Bending the knees so it turns into a squat.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Similar muscles; dumbbell instead of dumbbell.
Swap sheet: Less spinal loading, Less grip demand.
Swap sheet: Less stable, One side at a time, Less spinal loading.
Swap sheet: Heavier loading potential, More technical, Less grip demand.
